done_when: When the latest nightly full run failed, forge next names the platforms and failing tests and gives the forge fix start command for them

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Functional. For a fix found only on the remote, this line offers `forge work <fix>` when its status is `started` or `fixing`. `src/forge/worker.py:75-77` requires a local worktree and refuses that command when none exists. The named proof checks that the command is printed after removing the worktree, but never runs it. An agent following `forge next` cannot advance the existing fix.
findings.title: Not done: a fix started on another machine gets a command that cannot run

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Not done. The generated `forge fix start` command's `--done` text contains failed job names but none of the failing test IDs collected and printed above it. Starting that command therefore records no failing tests in the fix's acceptance condition. Earlier rounds raised this command clause for tests omitted after the tenth; the current command omits all of them, and the named proof expects that omission.
findings.title: Not done: When the latest nightly full run failed, forge next names the platforms and failing tests and gives the forge fix start command

stop.reason: Coordinator (Harm 2, reversible): the generated fix names the failed jobs and the run, not every test (forge next's lines already name every test); a fix started on another machine gets the plain line that it runs on that machine, like other remote items.

why: A failing nightly full run on macOS or Windows is easy to miss, and Windows stayed red for days unseen
